column1: # The test tracks of the Federation Tier with AQL specification, section 16.3,
# in specification order (#41). Tab-separated; lines starting with # are
# Derived columns: track, title, requirements, cps (the points whose tracks
# cell names the track). Hand-kept columns: status (covered, planned,
# deferred), issue, reason, with the same rules and the same deferral authority
# as conformance/matrix.tsv. Track 8 is deferred from the start: section 16.3
# marks it provisional and section 18 lets its subject matter be deferred.

column7: scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes of the harness: a plain patient AQL by POST and by GET answers one RESULT_SET validated against the vendored schema, with the client columns only, every row an ordered array, the additions nested under meta.federation, and columns[] the same whichever node answers first

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes with the harness PIX Manager as resolver: both carriers resolve to the same rows, each node is asked by its own ehr_id and its AQL carries no subject, a selected subject column is the re-injected input, and a member where the patient does not resolve is never asked

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes: ENDPOINT and ORGANISATION directives select the node set and report the rest excluded, a named member where the patient does not resolve is not-resolved, the endpoint header selects what the directive selects and a conflict is a 400, ?endpoint= targets nothing, and the PIXm localizer names the members asked and fails closed when it cannot answer

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes with faults at the capturing proxy: an error is 424 node-error, an unreachable node 504 offline, a slow node 504 time-out at the per-node timeout with latency_ms reported, a client wait shortens and never extends the budget, partial answers 200 only where offered, and found-nowhere and consent-denied are 200

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes holding the same composition: duplicates pass through by default, DISTINCT, ORDER BY and LIMIT apply over the union with OFFSET never pushed down, and an undirected COUNT is recombined or refused 400 while a directed one is answered; the opt-in object_id dedup of an imported copy is scored over mock nodes

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes: a follow-up read of a row reaches the CDR that holds it with its uid unchanged, an unseen ehr_id is probed read-only while a write to it is refused 400 and never probed, a new EHR is created at the one node named, and a versioned write reaches only its controlling node; CP-14 is deferred on the contradiction recorded on #212 (#354), CP-20 is an operator point, and CP-29 is scored over mock nodes

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes: the caller authenticates, each node receives the token its token endpoint issued for a client assertion verified against the published JWK Set and a signed token naming the caller, on the query and the follow-up, and consent is exercised with no consent service, with the development pre-filter denying and admitting, and on a directed query, with the refusal answered at node B proxy; CP-18 and CP-19 are node points and CP-39 an operator point

provisional in section 16.3, and section 18 lets its subject matter be deferred; the binding lifetime, the invalidation hook and the PMIR ITI-94 subscription that drives it from ITI-93 merges are built (#48, #147), and propagation to a later resolution is not claimed

scenario over the two FerroEHR nodes: a plain client given only a prefixed base reads and writes, both addressing forms answer the same rows, OPTIONS lists the members, DEMOGRAPHIC answers 501 as declared, a template list routes to the one named node, and a stored query is held at the gateway, runs by name over both members, refuses a second PUT, and a definition fan-out reports a one-node failure as 207

the gateway half is scored: the four positions on the fan-out, a directed query and the single-node route, and the converse write, judged on node-side capture over two mock nodes and over the two FerroEHR nodes of the harness; CP-27, the N34 obligation of the node itself, is scored by the node profile (#93)

the gateway half is scored over the two FerroEHR nodes of the harness: one ehr_id seeded at both for two patients is a 409 listing both claimants with one integrity incident, on a read and a scoped query the ask-all probe finds, and on a read and two writes the ehr_id index finds after its insert alarm, with no row served and no write applied; a versioned write no earlier step routes is a 400 and probes nobody; the admission half (CP-33a) is applied by the harness as the federation operator: a FerroEHR candidate sharing a member's system_id is refused by the registry load as a duplicate, and failed by the admission check under a system_id of its own
